## Let's do some exploratory data analyses (EDA) on my Harbour data. 
EDA is the process of exploring a dataset, coming to understand its features and structure, identify errors and outliers, understand the distribution and properties of variables and the relationships between them.

### Setting up my Workspace 
```{r}
# install.packages("arrow")
# install.packages("mice")
# install.packages("modelsummary")
# install.packages("naniar")
```

```{r}
library(arrow)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(mice)
library(modelsummary)
library(naniar)
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)
```

To get a quick sense of my data, I'll run the head() and tail() functions, then a random selection. 

```{r}

  head()
```
```{r}

```
```{r}

```
The first thing that is clear to me in doing this is the number of NR ("non-response") values my dataset has. The most important thing about doing this EDA will be for me to decide how to work around those missing values. I will return to this. 

Now, summary() will give the key summary statistics of my dataset. 
```{r}
harbourdatafinal |>
  summary()
```

The first thing I am going to do in order to make things easier for myself (I realize I had previously been over complicating this) is to remove a bunch of the columns. 

```{r}

    Inh_Benzos, Inh_Hydromorphone, Inh_Heroin, Inh_Methadone,
    Inh_Oxy, Inh_Prescription_Opioids, Inh_Amphetamines, Inh_Mixed,
```

Before I figure out what to do about the NAs, I am going to make the categorical variables and ordinal variables into factors.
First is slept last night. 
```{r}
harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Sleep_Last_Night <- factor(
  harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Sleep_Last_Night,
  levels = c("SH", "ST", "T", "FH", "RH", "SO", "AH"),
  labels = c(
    "Shelter",
    "Street",
    "Tent",
    "Friend's Home",
    "Recovery House",
    "Sobering House",
    "Apartment/House"
  )
)

```

```{r}
table(harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Sleep_Last_Night, useNA = "ifany")
is.ordered(harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Sleep_Last_Night)
```

Next is frequency of visits to The Harbour. 
```{r}
harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Freq_Harbour <- factor(
  harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Freq_Harbour,
  levels = c("FRS", "OC", "OPW", "FEW", "OPD", "M"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
table(harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Freq_Harbour, useNA = "ifany")
is.ordered(harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Freq_Harbour)
```
Next, time to Harbour is a little more difficult. 
```{r}
table(harbourdatafinaltrimmed$Time_To_Harbour, useNA = "ifany")
```
Here is a big code chunk that AI wrote for me. Let's see what it does....
```{r}
harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest <- harbourdatafinaltrimmed %>%
  mutate(
    # Step 1: Trim any hidden leading/trailing spaces
    clean_raw = trimws(as.character(Time_To_Harbour)),
    
    # Step 2: Group into clean categories
    Time_Category = case_when(
      # Group 1: 15 minutes or less (includes 0, ranges <= 15, and "Few")
      clean_raw %in% c(
        "0", "no time - live on same street (0)", "0 to 15",
        "1", "1 to 10", "1 to 15", "2", "3", "5", "5 to 10",
        "6", "6 to 8 min", "7", "8", "10", "10 to 15 min",
        "13", "15", "15 or less", "Few"
      ) ~ "15 mins or less",
      
      # Group 2: 16 to 30 minutes (includes ranges up to 30 and midpoints around 18-30)
      clean_raw %in% c(
        "1 to 25 min", "18", "20", "21", "25", "30", "5 to 30"
      ) ~ "16 to 30 mins",
      
      # Group 3: 31 to 60 minutes (includes ranges spanning up to 60 and "2 min or 1 hr")
      clean_raw %in% c(
        "10 to 60", "15 to 60", "30 to 60", "40", "45", 
        "5 to 60", "60", "2 min or 1 hr"
      ) ~ "31 to 60 mins",
      
      # Group 4: Over 60 minutes (includes >60 mins, "1 to 180", and "Hours")
      clean_raw %in% c(
        "65", "69", "120", "135", "1 to 180", 
        "240 or 540 (see note)", "Hours"
      ) ~ "Over 60 mins",
      
      # Group 5: Unspecified / Vague valid responses (15 rows total)
      # Note: Set to NA_character_ instead if you want to exclude these from analysis
      clean_raw %in% c("Minutes", "Minuites", "minuites", "Depends") ~ "~5 mins",
      
      # Group 6: Non-response and missing values (28 rows total)
      clean_raw %in% c("NR", "NR (see note)") | is.na(clean_raw) ~ NA_character_,
      
      # Safety catch: flags anything unexpected
      TRUE ~ "CHECK_ME"
    ),
    
    # Step 3: Convert to an ordered categorical factor
    Time_Category = factor(
      Time_Category,
      levels = c(
        "15 mins or less",
        "16 to 30 mins",
        "31 to 60 mins",
        "Over 60 mins",
        "~5 mins"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-clean_raw) # Remove temporary helper column

# Verify the final counts
table(harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest$Time_Category, useNA = "ifany")

```

I definitely not write that code on my own but I can somewhat understand it, at least. I decided to change the minutes type to "~5 mins" because I didn't want it to be lost or "unspecified" as AI suggested. 

Next, using supplies at The Harbour will be the same method as the frequency one. Lets see if I can write it myself. 

The harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest (I will change this name later) accidentally ended up overriding the df. This should fix it. I had to rerun the chunk above where I named it and delete the one that broke it and then it worked. 
```{r}
harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest$Supplies_Harbour <- factor(
  harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest$Supplies_Harbour,
  levels = c("N", "S", "A"),
  labels = c("Never", "Sometimes", "Always"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
table(harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest$Supplies_Harbour, useNA = "ifany")

is.ordered(harbourdatafinaltrimmedtest$Supplies_Harbour)
```
That is all the ordered variables. 

Now, I am not totally sure if there is a better way to be working with the gender, race, transportation and motivation variables other than a column per response option. For now, I'm going to move on to dealing with the NAs.
